title: Monitoring Robustness and Individual Fairness

problem.claim: Automated decision-makers should remain robust to slight input perturbations, including forms such as adversarial robustness, semantic robustness, and individual fairness.

gap.claim: Existing fixed-radius nearest-neighbor methods lack suitable online solutions for runtime monitoring.

contributions.claim: A runtime-monitoring approach for detecting input-output robustness violations in deployed black-box AI models from one long execution sequence.
Clemont, a tool providing lightweight monitors, including monitors based on upgraded online FRNN algorithms and a binary-decision-diagram-based algorithm.
A parallelization technique for monitors using the L∞ distance between input-output pairs.

stated_novelty.claim: One Clemont monitor uses an explicitly novel algorithm based on binary decision diagrams.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their parallelization technique can substantially reduce monitor computation time for L∞-based distances.
On standard benchmarks covering adversarial robustness, semantic robustness, and individual fairness, the authors report that Clemont monitors effectively detect robustness violations at runtime.

narrative_sequence.summary: Input-output robustness is presented as a desirable property with several forms in prior literature.
The paper proposes runtime monitoring of robustness in deployed black-box models to complement offline robustification.
The monitoring problem is formulated as FRNN search, and Clemont provides lightweight monitors plus parallelization for L∞-based distances.
Different Clemont monitors are compared on standard robustness and fairness benchmarks for runtime violation detection.

source_observation.claim: Runtime monitoring can identify when similar inputs produce dissimilar outputs during a model's execution.

interpretation.claim: Online behavioral checks can complement offline robustness-improvement methods for deployed black-box systems.

application.claim: Use runtime monitoring when deployment-time behavior may differ from what offline robustness analysis captures.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the monitor's detection guarantees, thresholds, or behavior outside the evaluated settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results or benchmark names.
The abstract does not specify monitor overhead, detection latency, false-positive behavior, or formal guarantees.
The abstract does not detail the novel algorithm or the online FRNN variants.
